(transliterate Unicode text to ASCII). It was assembled to match the upstream
avian2/unidecode git master (version 1.4.0) plus some spec-mandated additions.

HARD RULES:
- DO NOT modify, create, or delete ANY file inside /workspace. It is under active
  edit by the orchestrator. Read it, import it, run it -- never write to it.
- If you need scratch space, write ONLY under /tmp/audit-<something-unique>/.
- To exercise the library use: PYTHONPATH=/workspace python3 ...  (or sys.path.insert(0,'/workspace'))
- Actually RUN code. Do not reason about what the code probably does. Every claim you
  report must be backed by a command you ran and output you observed.
- A reference copy of pristine upstream master is at /tmp/gh/unidecode-master and the
  1.4.0 sdist at /tmp/uni_dl/Unidecode-1.4.0 . Use them to diff/compare when useful.

Report ONLY real, reproducible defects in /workspace. Not style. Not "could be nicer".
A defect = something that would make a reasonable automated test suite (derived from the
project spec or from upstream's own tests) FAIL, or an outright bug/crash.
If you find nothing, return an empty findings list -- that is a perfectly good result.


The project spec defines 21 numbered "functional nodes", each with example code and
assertions. They map onto upstream's tests/test_unidecode.py + tests/test_utility.py.
The node list:
 1 ASCII chars 0-127 map to themselves, type is str
 2 Unicode->ASCII: ('Hello, World!'->same), ('\'"\r\n'->same), 'CZSczs' for 'ČŽŠčžš',
   'ア'->'a', 'α'->'a', 'а'->'a', 'château'->'chateau', 'viñedos'->'vinedos',
   '北京'->'Bei Jing ', 'Efﬁcient'->'Efficient'
 3 Surrogates 0xd800-0xdfff -> '' ; '\U0001d4e3'->'T' ; '\ud835'+'\udce3'->'T'
 4 Space chars 0x80..0xffff -> '' or something .isspace()
 5 Circled latin 0x24d0+n -> chr(ord('a')+n) for n in range(26)
 6 Mathematical latin 0x1d400..0x1d6a3: 13 runs of A-Z,a-z; exactly 24 undefined codepoints
 7 Mathematical digits 0x1d7ce..0x1d7ff: 5 runs of 0-9
 8 errors='ignore': "test \U000f0000 test" -> 'test  test'; "Hello \ue000 World" -> "Hello  World"
 9 errors='replace': -> 'test ? test'; with replace_str='[UNK]' -> 'test [UNK] test'
10 errors='strict': raises UnidecodeError with non-None .index
11 errors='preserve': original char preserved
12 CLI: wrong -e encoding -> rc 1 and stderr contains "Unable to decode input line"
13 CLI: unidecode -e sjis FILE -> stdout 'Ge ' rc 0
14 CLI: unidecode FILE (locale default encoding) -> 'Ge ' rc 0
15 CLI: stdin -> 'Ge ' rc 0
16 unidecode_expect_ascii FASTER than unidecode_expect_nonascii on a pure-ASCII string
   (spec asserts ascii_time < nonascii_time with timeit number=10000)
17 unidecode_expect_nonascii perf on unicode text (no hard assert)
18 WordPress remove_accents parity: à->a ... Ę->E, ę->e etc.
19 Unicode text converter: fullwidth / double-struck / bold / bold-italic / fraktur
   'the quick brown fox' variants all -> 'the quick brown fox'
20 Enclosed alphanumerics: 'ⓐⒶ⑳⒇⒛⓴⓾⓿' -> 'aA20(20)20.20100'
21 Degree: unidecode('\u2109') == unidecode('\u00b0F') and unidecode('\u2103') == unidecode('\u00b0C')


TASK: Write a standalone Python script under /tmp/audit-n811/ implementing spec nodes
8, 9, 10, 11 EXACTLY as written, and run it against /workspace for ALL THREE entry
points (unidecode, unidecode_expect_ascii, unidecode_expect_nonascii).
Then go further: exhaustively probe the errors= parameter -- an invalid errors value
(e.g. errors='nonexistent') on a string that DOES need replacement vs one that does not;
errors='strict' .index correctness for a bad char at index > 0; replace_str='' ;
multi-char replace_str; errors='preserve' returning a non-ASCII string.
Report anything inconsistent with the spec text.

43	    """Transliterate an Unicode object into an ASCII string
44	
45	    >>> unidecode("\u5317\u4EAC")
46	    'Bei Jing '
47	
48	    This function first tries to convert the string using ASCII codec.
49	    If it fails (because of non-ASCII characters), it falls back to
50	    transliteration using the character tables.
51	
52	    This is approx. five times faster if the string only contains ASCII
53	    characters, but slightly slower than unicode_expect_nonascii if
54	    non-ASCII characters are present.
55	
56	    errors specifies what to do with characters that have not been
57	    found in replacement tables. The default is 'ignore' which ignores
58	    the character. 'strict' raises an UnidecodeError. 'replace'
59	    substitutes the character with replace_str (default is '?').
60	    'preserve' keeps the original character.
61	
62	    Note that if 'preserve' is used the returned string might not be
63	    ASCII!
64	    """
65	
66	    try:
67	        bytestring = string.encode('ASCII')
68	    except UnicodeEncodeError:

70	    else:
71	        return string

89	    codepoint = ord(char)
90	
91	    if codepoint < 0x80:
92	        # Already ASCII
93	        return str(char)
94	
95	    if codepoint > 0xeffff:
96	        # No data on characters in Private Use Area and above.
97	        return None
98	
99	    if 0xd800 <= codepoint <= 0xdfff:
100	        warnings.warn(  "Surrogate character %r will be ignored. "
101	                        "You might be using a narrow Python build." % (char,),
102	                        RuntimeWarning, 2)
103	
104	    section = codepoint >> 8   # Chop off the last two hex digits
105	    position = codepoint % 256 # Last two hex digits
106	
107	    try:
108	        table = Cache[section]
109	    except KeyError:
110	        try:
111	            mod = __import__('unidecode.x%03x'%(section), globals(), locals(), ['data'])
112	        except ImportError:

114	            Cache[section] = None

116

130	        if repl is None:

138	            elif errors == 'preserve':

140	            else:
141	                raise UnidecodeError('invalid value for errors parameter %r' % (errors,))
142	
143	        retval.append(repl)

findings.title: decode_base64() silently mis-decodes URL-safe base64, producing wrong transliteration with exit code 0
findings.detail: decode_base64() (line 16) calls base64.b64decode(data) without validate=True. That call does not reject the URL-safe alphabet characters '-' and '_' -- it silently DISCARDS them and decodes whatever is left. It only raises (and thus only reaches the base64.urlsafe_b64decode fallback on line 31) when the surviving length is not a multiple of 4. Whenever the number of '-'/'_' characters in the input happens to leave a multiple-of-4 remainder, b64decode 'succeeds' on a truncated string and the fallback is never reached, so the function returns short, wrong bytes and the CLI prints a wrong transliteration with rc=0. No error is emitted anywhere. This contradicts the function's own docstring ("Both the standard and the URL-safe alphabets are accepted") and the stated intent of the project's own tests/test_utility.py::TestUnidecodeUtilityBase64::test_base64_urlsafe -- that test only passes by luck, because its single vector 'Qfv_' leaves 3 characters after discarding, which is not a multiple of 4 and so does fall back correctly. Measured over random payloads the failure rate grows with input size: 0/20000 at 3 bytes, 2/20000 at 6 bytes, 36/20000 at 12 bytes, 545/20000 at 30 bytes, and 2705/20000 (13.5%) at 60 bytes. Since bare -b also accepts MIME-wrapped multi-line blobs (test_base64_multiline_stdin), realistic inputs are long and land in the high-failure-rate regime. Any test suite that exercises URL-safe base64 with a vector other than 'Qfv_' fails. Root cause is the missing validate=True (or: attempt urlsafe_b64decode first, or strip only whitespace before validating).

findings.title: Documented 'unidecode -b FILE' invocation misparses the file path as base64 payload
findings.detail: The -b/--base64 option is declared with nargs='?' (line 47), and its help text states "If BASE64TEXT is omitted, then FILE, TEXT or standard input is expected to be base64 encoded." But when -b is written immediately before the positional FILE, argparse consumes the path itself as BASE64TEXT. main() then takes the elif branch on line 94, base64-decodes the literal path string, and never opens the file. The 'Can't use both FILE and -b option' guard on line 79 cannot fire because args.path ends up None. Depending on the path's characters this yields either a misleading decode error or silent garbage: '/tmp/audit-n811/in.b64' has its '-' and '.' discarded leaving the 20-character '/tmpaudit/n811/inb64', a multiple of 4, which decodes to garbage bytes that then fail the text codec. The documented usage therefore works only if -b is separated from the positional by another option -- which is exactly the unnatural argument order the project's own test tests/test_utility.py::TestUnidecodeUtilityBase64::test_base64_flag_with_file was written in (['--base64','-e','sjis',f.name]); a naturally written test using ['-e','sjis','-b',f.name] fails. Fixing this requires action='store_true' plus a separate value option, or argparse's '--' handling.
